comment: As currently framed, the guidance prioritizes technical data transmission capability without explicitly linking exchange to clinical-economic workflow resolution. Data exchange is clinically and economically neutral without clinical transaction resolution. In both high- and low-resource settings, the highest leverage lies in managing treatment adherence and preventing chronic disease progression (e.g., managing hypertension and early-stage kidney disease to avoid stroke or end-stage renal disease). Unclosed care loops create administrative noise, increase clinical burden, and result in a net-negative return on public infrastructure investment.

public.suggestedRevision: Insert under Section 1.3 (Design Principles): “As a core design principle, DPI-H should prioritize the clinical-economic resolution of workflows alongside technical data exchange. The architecture should be designed to deliver system-level clinical outcomes and prevent chronic disease progression (such as tracking medication adherence to prevent stroke, managing early-stage chronic kidney disease to avoid end-stage renal disease, and supporting hypertension treatment control) rather than optimizing for technical transmission capability alone.”
